paragraphs: Friend, look at how much came at David in one chapter. A king's order, a spear, messengers watching his house, and three teams of messengers sent to seize him. Not one of them got him, and Saul had the crown and the spear. That's the lesson sitting right on top of this passage (1 Samuel 19:1, 10, 11, 20-21).

Now look at HOW David got out. A friend, Jonathan, spoke up for him, and his wife, Michal, lowered him from a window (1 Samuel 19:4-5, 11-12). Then he went to Samuel, the prophet, and told him all that Saul had done to him (1 Samuel 19:18). I think that's worth holding onto, baker, because God's help doesn't always show up as a lightning bolt. Sometimes it shows up as a friend with a good plan and a window.

Then there's Saul. He swore an oath, and then he threw a spear (1 Samuel 19:6, 10). He sent men to seize David, and the Spirit of God came upon them, and then upon Saul himself (1 Samuel 19:20-24). Some plans just can't win, and I'd rather be on the side that isn't fighting God. So if you're being chased by something bigger than you today, take heart, because the story between David and Saul is not over.
